publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovation in Engineering and Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Due to the increasing popularity and easy accessibility of social networking services, the number of users in social networks is increasing rapidly. As a result, their size and user-generated content are growing day-to-day. One of the requirements is to capture such a huge amount of data and analyze them for desired purposes, such as target marketing, recommender system design, open-source intelligence, and cybersecurity. Twitter is one of the most popular social network sites (aka microblogging site) and it is used by almost every person for the news update, information sharing, viral marketing, etc using 280 characters. In this paper, we have applied a text analytics framework to analyze Twitter data at different levels of granularity. One of the distinguishing features of the proposed framework is to exploit both content and structural information for tweets analysis. The proposed framework first models the tweets into a multi-attributed graph, wherein tweets are rep-resented as nodes and inter-tweet relationships are represented as edges. For node labeling, we have used NLP techniques to identify features from tweets, whereas edges are labeled using meta-data (such as hashtags, mentions, followers, etc.) that are common to the tweets connected by the edges. For analyzing the multi-attributed graph, we have considered two algorithms, MAG-Dist and MAG-Sim, to convert the multi-attributed graph into a simple and similarity graph. Finally, we have applied MCL (Markov Clustering) algorithm to cluster the nodes of the multi-attributed graph, each group consisting of a particular subset of tweets representing an event. The experimental evaluation of the proposed approach is done on a real dataset crawled from Twitter.

articleTitle: A Systematic Review on Hybrid Analysis using Machine Learning for Android Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovation in Engineering and Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Android is the most ubiquitous mobile operating system nowadays. It's prevalence also provokes the humongous growth of Android malware. Primarily researchers have focused on static and dynamic analysis using machine learning techniques to detect Android malware. But, multifarious evasion techniques by the shrewd malware authors have made those techniques limited and ineffective. Therefore, recent researchers have shifted their focus on discovering an effective strategy to fight against. Hybrid analysis: a fusion of static and dynamic analysis would be a good candidate for that as it prevails over the individual drawbacks of static and dynamic analysis with the cost of complexity. According to research, hybrid analysis has many opportunities as well as challenges. This work aims at presenting a thorough and systematic review of hybrid analysis using machine learning techniques for Android malware detection. It encompasses the leading researches on hybrid analysis: their contributions, strengths, and weaknesses. This work also discusses the challenges, opportunities and future directions of hybrid analysis for Android malware detection.

articleTitle: Implementing Large Enterprise Resource Planning Systems with Agile Methods
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovation in Engineering and Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Agile methods, when applied to the implementation of large enterprise resource planning (ERP) system projects, present several benefits over traditional non-agile approaches. This study presents several established models for applying Agile to large projects, and then it shows in details how to apply Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) to a large ERP implementation. This study also discusses the critical success factors required for maximizing success in ERP implementation. The study utilizes a multi-vocal literature review to develop a scholar-practitioner view of an ERP system, and then it combines that perspective with our own experience in implementing large ERP projects using SAFe. To the best of our knowledge, this study is a first in establishing SAFe for the implementation of large ERP projects.

articleTitle: Use of nanoparticles arrays made of alloys of plasmonic metals of varying compositions to enhance the opto-electronic performance of thin-film solar cells
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovation in Engineering and Technology (ICIET)
abstract: The demand for the photovoltaic (PV) cells has increased exponentially in the last decade as solar energy has become extremely popular because it is environmentally friendly and relatively affordable, thus making solar energy an attractive alternative to fossil fuels. Of the many methods available to increase the efficiency/performance of PV cells, the use of plasmonic nanostructures have been have been a major focus of recent research due to their ability to significantly enhance the light absorption and other optical/electrical performance of solar cells. In this paper, plasmonic metal nanoparticles made of alloys of silver, aluminum and gold with different percentage in their composition were used to enhance the opto-electronic performance of thin-film solar cells. The alloys were studied in an attempt to harness the favorable plasmon enhancement properties of individual silver, gold and aluminum particles and create a more efficient enhancing material. The size and pitch (the edge-to-edge distance between adjacent nanoparticles in an array) of the alloy nanoparticles in an array is also varied and analyzed. The simulation results show that an alloy made of Ag-Al(10%-90%) of 100nm diameter having a pitch of 100nm gives the most favorable result when compared to other composition of the alloys or with pure metal. This conclusion was reached through the analysis of optical absorption enhancement, open circuit voltage produced, short circuit current generation, fill factor calculations, efficiency and optical near-field optical enhancement studies.

articleTitle: P-Cloud - A cost efficient definitive cloud with user satisfaction using non-cloud resources
publicationTitle: 2019 2nd International Conference on Innovation in Engineering and Technology (ICIET)
abstract: Today is the age of Cloud Computing Technology in IT Industries. Cloud computing which is built on the Internet has the most robust architecture of computation. In this work, we have proposed a cloud infrastructure. P-Cloud (Personal Cloud) for leasing computing resources appending non-cloud resources such as laptops, PCs, clusters and enterprise servers. Generally, infrastructure resource providers are responsible for providing infrastructure resources, however, the proposed P-Cloud deals with personal resources. P-Cloud permits a huge number of excess computing resources, on the scale of hundreds of millions, to be leased out to cloud users. By sharing of such resources allows resource owners to earn from idle resources, and cloud users to have a cost-efficient auxiliary to vast cloud service providers. In this work, we mainly focus to develop strategies to make relations between the users and resource owners where the two have opposite goals as well as how to fulfill their requirements mainly user satisfaction and system profit. The proposed system makes a platform between the user group and the resource owner group. Finally, the proposed system is implemented in CloudSim Plus.
